pr.title: feat(shell): add setup --wrapper to install the stk function and its completion
pr.body: `git stk setup --wrapper` now installs the `stk` shell function alongside the completion line, and teaches the shell to complete `stk` the same way it completes `git-stk`. bash and zsh only — fish needs different syntax, and PowerShell declines with an explanation rather than writing shell-function syntax into `$PROFILE`. ### Decisions worth reviewing - **Opt-in.** It defines a new command name, so plain `setup` doesn't write it (and advertises the flag instead). Setup skips it, saying why, when an `stk` executable is on `PATH` or the rc already defines one — it never wins that collision. - **The completion alias is guarded.** Unguarded, `complete -p git-stk | sed …` prints `complete: git-stk: no completion specification` on *every shell start* whenever the registration is absent. Now a missing registration costs `stk` completion and nothing else. - **The block closes with `# end git-stk setup`.** This was the real hazard: `strip_completion_block` removed marker + one line, so `uninstall` would have left ~15 orphaned wrapper lines. Strip now removes the block whole, with a fallback to the old single-line shape so blocks written by 0.11.0/0.11.1 still uninstall cleanly. - **Re-running merges.** `setup -y` then `setup -y --wrapper` rewrites the one block instead of appending a second. If the completion line was hand-added without our marker, setup refuses to rewrite it and prints the wrapper to paste — the same policy `uninstall` already uses. ### Verification status bash is verified end to end: the generated block sourced in a real bash with `git-stk` on `PATH` (function defined, `complete -p stk` registered, `stk res` → `restack`, `stk up`/`down` crossing worktrees), sourced again with `PATH=/nonexistent` to confirm silence, and `uninstall` shown to lift all 19 lines while leaving surrounding user lines intact. The e2e commit's bash step was also extracted from the YAML and run verbatim against an Ubuntu-style early-returning `.bashrc`. **zsh and pwsh are not verified locally** — neither shell is installed on my machine, so their first real run is the next E2E dispatch. In particular the macOS cell asserts `compdef stk=git-stk` populates `$_comps[stk]`; if that mechanism is wrong for clap's dynamic zsh completion, that cell will fail and block the release. Worth a manual `workflow_dispatch` of E2E before tagging rather than finding out at release time. Fish has no cell in the e2e matrix, so its decline path is covered only by `tests/setup.rs`. - 🟣 ~~[feat(shell): add setup --wrapper to install the stk function and its completion (#299)](https://github.com/lararosekelley/git-stk/pull/299)~~ (merged) 👈 - 🟣 ~~[docs(shell): harden the stk wrapper snippet against a failed navigation (#298)](https://github.com/lararosekelley/git-stk/pull/298)~~ (merged) - `main` --- Stack managed by [git-stk](https://github.com/lararosekelley/git-stk)
